done_when: A Claude worker's fix round continues the session its first round started and gets only the short fix prompt; when that session can't be continued it starts fresh with the full brief and says so; tests run forge work twice on a Claude worker and check both paths

findings.body: Any nonzero exit from `claude --resume` is treated as proof that the session cannot continue when the checkout is unchanged. A valid resumed session can instead fail during its turn. Forge then starts another session with the full brief, discards the valid session record, and may repeat work. Claude's [error reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/errors) says an exit code alone does not identify the failure and warns that resending after a mid-response failure can repeat tool calls. Restart only for a resume failure, rather than every failed resumed turn.

findings.body: The new tests cover successful resumes and cases where Claude rejects a resume, but none covers a saved session that accepts `--resume` and then exits nonzero. A two-round `forge work` test using the existing stub with `STUB_CLAUDE_EXIT=3` on the second round would catch the unintended new session and repeated full brief. The current test's forced resume error cannot detect that behavior.
findings.title: Not done: a forge work test for failure during a valid Claude resume

findings.body: Ordinary Claude workers use `nullcontext` at `worker.py:81`. Two concurrent `forge work` calls can therefore both read this session record, resume the same ID, and write the same `rounds + 1` value at `worker.py:410`; one round is lost from the record. The writes also share the temporary record path used at `codex.py:463`. Apply the existing item lock to ordinary Claude rounds before reading and updating their session.
findings.title: Serialize ordinary Claude rounds that share a session record

why: Claude workers start a fresh session every round and get the whole brief again, so fix rounds lose the worker's context, unlike Codex workers
